51/S0.subgoal: Explain how the natural walking-speed model motivates optimizing VR navigation experience by limiting exposure duration to reduce cybersickness.

51/S1.subgoal: Describe the factors that determine VR exposure duration and the semi-interactive tour assumptions used to limit interaction time.

51/S2.subgoal: State the two path-optimization problems for controlling exposure duration: minimum time to visit all POIs or maximum POIs within a time limit.

51/S3.subgoal: Formulate the minimum-time all-POI tour problem as a weighted graph and state the path optimization objective.

51/S4.subgoal: Derive the travel-time estimate between directly connected POIs using the natural walking-speed model.

51/S5.subgoal: Explain how to sum edge travel times for a complete tour and transform the incomplete POI graph into a TSP instance with hypothetical shortest-path edges.

51/S6.subgoal: Describe the algorithm that converts the POI graph to a complete time-weighted TSP, solves it, and restores a valid original-graph path, while noting the cybersickness-threshold limitation.

51/S7.subgoal: Summarize the lecture’s graph-theoretic TSP approach and preview the next fixed-time, maximum-POI optimization problem.
